claims.text: ProductsController.List() builds a ProductDto for each row as new ProductDto(p.Id, p.Name, p.PriceVnd), read from a Product entity queried via db.Products.

DonHang.Api/Dtos.cs defines ProductDto(int Id, string Name, int PriceVnd), OrderItemDto(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd), OrderDto(...), CreateOrderItemRequest(...), and CreateOrderRequest(List<CreateOrderItemRequest> Items) as records.
The Product entity in DonHang.Domain has exactly the properties Id, Name, and PriceVnd, the same three ProductDto lists.
The OrderItem entity in DonHang.Domain has OrderId, ProductId, Quantity, and UnitPriceVnd; OrderItemDto omits OrderId, keeping only ProductId, Quantity, and UnitPriceVnd.
The Customer entity in DonHang.Domain has a PasswordHash property alongside FullName, Email, and City.

ASP.NET Core's default JSON options for Web API controllers set a camelCase naming policy for the response: the first word of each property name is lowercase, later words keep their capital (PriceVnd -> priceVnd). This is ASP.NET Core's web defaults, not System.Text.Json's own default behavior.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Web API serialization defaults (web defaults set PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase)

claims.text: Sending GET /api/v1/products/1 to the running stage-1 lab returns 200 with body {"id":1,"name":"Bàn phím cơ","priceVnd":1250000} — camelCase field names, not PascalCase.

Deserialization is not a strict mirror of serialization: ASP.NET Core's web defaults also set PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true, so a request body's field name may differ in case from the C# property and still bind to it.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Web API serialization defaults (web defaults set PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true)

claims.text: Returning the Customer entity from an endpoint serializes PasswordHash as a passwordHash field, including when it is null, because ASP.NET Core writes null properties by default.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Web API serialization defaults (no DefaultIgnoreCondition set)
